_readme: These are MEASURED baselines, not targets. Each number here was captured by actually
running the named command and reading its output on the date recorded in the entry's
Changing any number in this file is a deliberate act that belongs in the SAME commit as
whatever changed the underlying measurement (a fix, a new test, a dependency bump). This
file is never edited to make a red CI run go green without that accompanying change.
A DROP in a failure count is as much a reason to investigate as a RISE. A failure that
disappeared without a commit that fixed it is a signal, not a free pass — see voteEngine's
exact (not floor) check on both count and titles.
scripts/assert-ci-baselines.mjs reads this file by import.meta.url, never mutates it, and
has no 'update the baseline' mode. Updating a baseline is a human, reviewed commit.

voteEngine.note:
Re-measured 2026-09-01 for the @optimystic 0.24.2 -> 0.25.1 / p2p-fret beta.3 -> beta.4 bump. Live run: 1656 passing / 72 pending / 9 failing.

expectedFailing 8 -> 9. The added title is the THIRD P2P-11 residual tripwire ('no seeding path exists from a circuit-relay reservation into the peer address book'), which flipped on the bump. It is a source-SHAPE tripwire over installed db-p2p, not a behavioural test, and it flipped because 0.25.1 reshaped Libp2pKeyPeerNetwork.findCluster -- classifySelfDialability now splits the old `parsed.length === 0` count into `addressless` vs `selfRelayOnly`. The residual itself is NOT fixed: 0.25.1 still assigns the locally-parsed addresses straight into the record (libp2p-key-network.js:889) and still merely COUNTS addressless members (:886, :895) rather than seeding them. It is carried as a known failure rather than re-anchored because the spec's own sibling test demands a device n=4 re-proof before the assertions are rewritten against a new version -- that proof has not been run. Re-anchor all three P2P-11 tripwires together, after it.

SIX failures were RETIRED in this same commit, which is why 9 is not 15. Three were version pins reconciled to the new line (no-portal-vendor-regression PUB-01-c, and published-stack-lock-regression PUB-02 x2). Three were the gossipsub/libp2p-3 skew tripwires (post-peerId-patch blocker 3), whose subject db-p2p 0.25.1 removed outright -- the block was rewritten from 'the skew still exists' to 'gossipsub is absent and must not return', so the coverage is inverted, not deleted. The dead @chainsafe/libp2p-gossipsub yarn-patch resolution was dropped from root package.json in the same commit; the .patch file is retained on disk.

minPassing 1411 -> 1656 (ciMinPassing 1410 -> 1655). The 1411 figure was measured 2026-08-26 and had gone stale as later waves added tests, leaving the floor ~245 tests loose -- it would not have caught a mass disappearance. Raised to the live measurement here because this is already a reviewed baseline commit. The deliberate ciMinPassing = minPassing - 1 relationship is UNCHANGED and still has the same cause, restated: `.planning/` is a nested git repo the outer repo gitignores, so a fresh CI checkout never has it, and strand-cohort-routing-coverage.spec.ts's 'the diagnosis doc is present...' test calls this.skip() when absent -- reporting as pending on CI instead of passing. expectedFailing stays exactly 9 in BOTH environments; only the passing/pending split moves.

dashboardTier1.note:
Re-measured 2026-09-01 at 462 passing / 0 failing / ~21s wall, raising minPassing from 444. The floor is raised here because the checker's own notice asked for it deliberately, and because this commit is the one that returns the gate to zero failures: capabilities.js had been stale against votetorrent.qsql since 2026-08-27, when 97acf6f0 (AssociationRequest) and 0da5b2bd (ElectionRecordValidityPolicy) added scope-enforcement sites and 745a1e57 regenerated schema-sql.ts without regenerating the capability matrix. Total enforcement sites 41 -> 45 (vrg 16 -> 18, mel 10 -> 12). Note that regenerating ALONE takes this gate from 1 failure to 5: the generated file is a hub, and src/reads/registrations.js's hand-maintained SURFACE_COUNT_QUERIES map had silently lost lockstep with the DERIVED TABLES_READ, so the new vrg table reached db.prepare(undefined). Original note follows.

Nyquist gap-closure round 4 (2026-08-26), FINAL STATE 444 pass / 0 fail: the escalated implementation fix landed in this same commit -- DashboardShell.tsx:623 now logs `console.error(err.name)` only, matching its three siblings at :394/:584/:608, so the deliberately-red widened matcher is green and minPassing/maxFailing were returned to 444/0 exactly as the escalation required. Re-measured live after the fix: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/node/*.test.mjs` -> 444 pass / 0 fail / ~20.6s wall. The intermediate 443/1 state described below is retained for the record because it documents WHY the matcher was widened and what it caught. Original round-4 note follows: raised 439 -> 444 total (443 pass / 1 fail), re-measured live via `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/node/*.test.mjs` three times (~19.5-20.1s wall each). GAP 1 (D-03) added test/node/no-qr-affordance.test.mjs, 5 new cases: a positive control against a planted QR/camera sentinel, an inertness control, the self-tripping-trap proof (DashboardSignInCodeScreen.tsx's own D-03 comment matches the RAW source but not the comment-stripped source), and the real absence scan over both sign-in surfaces (Bootstrap.tsx + apps/VoteTorrentAuthority/src/screens/dashboard/*.tsx) -- all 5 pass. GAP 4 (RF-03) widened shell-wiring.test.mjs's RAW_MESSAGE_RE from the narrow `err instanceof Error ? err.message` ternary shape to any bare `err(or)?.message` token inside a console.error(...) call -- this correctly and deliberately turns 'no panel and not the shell logs a raw database error MESSAGE to the console' RED, naming DashboardShell.tsx (the real site is :623, `console.error(err.name, err.message)`, which the old matcher's ternary-only shape could not see). maxFailing raised 0 -> 1 and minPassing 439 -> 443 (the passing count, not the total) to reflect this ONE deliberately-red, escalated test -- it is not a regression and must not be silenced by weakening the matcher; it should return to maxFailing: 0 / minPassing: 444 in the SAME commit that makes DashboardShell.tsx:623 log `err.name` only, matching its three siblings. See VALIDATION.md's GAP 4 entry for the escalation. GAP 2 (D-18 browser leg, WR-04/RF-04) and GAP 3 (RF-01) added no test:node cases -- their evidence lives in test/browser/compose-gate.tsx (PHASE 10's new rungs 9-12) and apps/VoteTorrentDashboard/scripts/assert-no-test-harness-in-dist.mjs respectively, so this count is unaffected by either. Prior history retained verbatim below. 50-04's original local budget was 5s at 12 tests. The suite has grown to 326 tests across 50-05/50-08/50-09/50-12, and a live re-run during 50-13 measured ~17.5s internal / ~18s wall on this machine three times in a row. maxSeconds was therefore set to 45 (not the phase-history figure of 15, which is now stale and would fail on a clean run before any CI slowness is even added) to give real CI headroom over the current measured cost. The bound exists to keep tier 1 a fast gate -- exceeding it is a signal the tier is drifting into something else, not a number to raise reflexively. See the 50-13 SUMMARY's Deviations section for the full measurement. Raised 326 -> 330 by the code-review fix for CR-01, which added four assertions to test/node/preview-control.test.mjs (the re-seed matcher, its inertness control, the dead-prop matcher and its inertness control) -- re-measured live at 330 pass / 0 fail / ~19.5s in the same commit that added them. Raised 330 -> 332 by the fix for WR-02, which added a copyKeyForPhase totality test and its unmapped-phase control, then 332 -> 334 by WR-04 (the relabelled-envelope refusal and its clean-bootstrap positive control) 334 -> 335 by WR-05 (the blocked-delete record-survival test) 335 -> 337 by WR-06 (the non-creating listObjectStores probe and its present-database positive control) and 337 -> 341 by WR-10 (the new test/node/shell-wiring.test.mjs source suite, two matchers plus two inertness controls), then 341 -> 344 by WR-11 (the handle-handover matcher, its close-after inertness control and the both-call-sites check), then 344 -> 347 by WR-12 (panel console hygiene, its inertness control and the nine-site count) and 347 -> 350 by WR-16 (the banner-default matcher, its old-shape inertness control and the distinct-copy check) 350 -> 351 by WR-17 (the applied-count test) and 351 -> 355 by WR-18 (the empty-expected-name refusal, its non-empty positive control, and the shell-side guard plus its inertness control). Raised 355 -> 364 by 50-14 Task 1's CR-01 gap closure: 9 new `resyncRealScopes` cases in test/node/preview-scopes.test.mjs (referential stability, the CR-01 empty-to-nine transition, the sticky touched guard plus its positive control, order-insensitivity, duplicates, validation parity, and the frozen/no-mutation check) -- re-measured live at 364 pass / 0 fail / ~18-19s wall in the same commit range that added them. preview-control.test.mjs's existing assertions were updated in place (not added), so its count is unchanged. Raised 364 -> 370 by 50-16's gap-closure plan: Task 1 added 5 new refresh-swap.test.mjs cases proving the CR-02 repair path (an explicit-empty-counts variant of the row-count record, a genuine post-swap divergence, the unheld-network throw, a storage-sequence-log proof of read-after-write with zero extra writes, and a direct write-count assertion on a verify-failed refusal), and Task 2's copy.test.mjs rewrite net +1 (two copyKeyForPhase tests replaced by three: the mechanical bootstrap.phase.<value> coverage test, its unmapped-key throw, and a new panelFrame.*Pill interpolation test) -- re-measured live at 370 pass / 0 fail / ~19.8s wall in the same commit range that added them. Raised 370 -> 372 by 50-17 Task 1's WR-06 gap-closure: two new db-delete.test.mjs cases (the immediately-after-deleteNetworkDb listObjectStores sequence, and the indexedDB.databases()-unavailable fallback branch actually being entered) -- re-measured live at 372 pass / 0 fail / ~19.9-23.0s wall (three consecutive local runs) in the same commit that added them. Raised 372 -> 399 by 50-18's D-14 gap closure: 27 new cases -- bootstrap-redemption.test.mjs gained 21 (the already-bootstrapped networkHash assertion, the D-14 single-flight-replay seam test, and 19 source-level wiring tests + inertness controls for Bootstrap.tsx's three new optional props and main.tsx's onComplete/onAlreadyBootstrapped wiring and zero-timer state); refresh-swap.test.mjs gained 20 minus 14 net (two WR-11 behavioural close-forwarding tests, two per-hop source-pin tests plus an inertness control, and 12 DashboardShell.tsx source-wiring tests + inertness controls for the new pendingSwapContext classify effect) -- re-measured live at 399 pass / 0 fail / ~20.0s wall in the same commit range that added them. Raised 399 -> 439 by this gap-closure round's three parallel plans (50-20/50-22/50-23), consolidated into ONE re-measurement here per this round's own plan sequencing (50-24 was scoped to defer the baseline bump until after all three landed): 50-20 added the makeFakeTransport singleUse fixture tests plus the Bootstrap.tsx handedOffRef wiring tests (D-14/CR-02); 50-22 added the classify() catch/swap-error-banner tests, the handed-off-transport reset-coverage tests, and the withNetworkDbLifecycleLock lock-coverage tests over forgetNetwork/performOfficerSwap (CR-03/CR-04); 50-23 added the scopesResolved context/control wiring tests and the DashboardShell reset-block/provider-prop wiring tests (CR-01/D-18). 50-24 itself (this plan) added no new test:node cases -- its own new coverage is entirely in the browser gate (compose-gate.tsx's wire-call-count rungs and the new compose-preview-race phase, run-headless.mjs's --swap-only flag and PHASE 10) -- so this bump reflects only the prior three plans' work, re-measured live and unchanged by anything in this commit's own diff. Re-measured live at 439 pass / 0 fail / ~20.6s wall (`time yarn workspace votetorrent-dashboard test:node`, internal duration_ms ~19844-20077 across three consecutive local runs) in this commit. Gap-closure round 3's code-review fixes (CR-01 stale swapError, CR-02 double-confirm double-spend, WR-10 double-forget) added NO test:node cases and minPassing therefore stays at 439 -- re-measured live at 439 pass / 0 fail / ~20.4-20.5s wall across two runs in this commit range, NOT assumed unchanged. That is deliberate rather than an oversight: round 3's own WR-06 found that roughly 30 of the 40 tier-1 cases added the round before are `assert.match` regexes against a `.tsx` file read as a STRING, and neither Critical it found has a source-text signature -- state that is never written, and a handler that runs twice. Adding more matchers of that kind would have raised this number without raising coverage. The new evidence is entirely behavioural and lives in the browser gate: compose-gate.tsx's new compose-guards phase (PHASE 11, plus run-headless.mjs --guards-only, 14 rungs, two real networks) mounts the production DashboardShell and drives the actual state transitions, and each of its three discriminating rungs was measured in BOTH directions against a deliberately reverted fix. One of them was measured INERT on its first attempt and rewritten (waitForOrTimeout) rather than reported -- see the CR-02 commit message.

authorityTypecheck.note: This is a ceiling, not a floor: the producer half added to apps/VoteTorrentAuthority by this phase must introduce none. A drop below 51 means someone fixed something and the ceiling should be lowered in that same commit, not silently absorbed.

voterJest.reason: This phase (the authority web dashboard) touches nothing in apps/VoteTorrentVoter. Importing an unrelated red baseline into a gate whose whole value is trustworthiness would make the gate less useful, not more. Recorded here, and echoed to every CI run's job summary, precisely so it cannot be silently forgotten -- it is not this phase's to fix, and it is not this workflow's to run.
